opportunities.title: Make campus a little kinder.
opportunities.description: Turn a student pain point into a thoughtful little design. No portfolio required, just a curious mind.

opportunities.title: Code something that matters.
opportunities.description: Start a tiny tool that makes someone's everyday easier. Big impact can start with a very small idea.

opportunities.title: A greener corner of campus.
opportunities.description: Find one small way to make your campus more sustainable, then sketch a plan to make it happen.

opportunities.title: Give a good story a voice.
opportunities.description: Practice telling a story that deserves to be heard. Start with someone who inspires you.

opportunities.title: Learn a little. Build a lot.
opportunities.description: Explore a fictional introductory class and turn one concept into something you can explain.

opportunities.title: Find your people, find your spark.
opportunities.description: Try a sample student club challenge. Practice showing up with an idea and a little curiosity.

opportunities.title: Turn curiosity into a new skill.
opportunities.description: Preview a fictional certification path. Build a study plan before committing to a course.

opportunities.title: Make room for a new perspective.
opportunities.description: Prepare for a fictional local career event. Get clear on what you would like to learn.

opportunities.title: One conversation can open a door.
opportunities.description: Practice introducing yourself with a fictional networking prompt. No messages are sent.

opportunities.title: Try on a career for a little while.
opportunities.description: Take on a fictional product team scenario and practice making a decision with limited information.

opportunities.title: Your next chapter starts before you apply.
opportunities.description: Prepare for a fictional internship. Identify what you can already show and one thing you could strengthen.

quests.title: Find one tiny friction
quests.description: Good design starts with noticing. Turn an everyday frustration into a possibility.
steps: Notice one thing on campus that could be easier.
Write down who it affects and why it matters.
Sketch one possible solution on paper. Keep it simple.

quests.title: Sketch your tiny tool
quests.description: Before the first line of code, give your idea a little shape.
steps: Choose a small problem you or a friend faces.
Write one sentence describing your tool.
Draw the main screen and label its three most useful features.

quests.title: Spot a greener possibility
quests.description: Small observations can grow into meaningful change.
steps: Find one place on campus where resources are wasted.
Write down a practical improvement.
List one person or campus group who could help.

quests.title: Write a six-sentence story
quests.description: You do not need a whole novel to make someone feel something.
steps: Choose a fictional student doing something kind.
Write six sentences: a beginning, a challenge, and a hopeful ending.
Read it aloud and improve one sentence.

quests.title: Notice one little thing
quests.description: A two-minute step is enough. You can return to this practice every day.
steps: Look around and notice one thing that could be easier.
Write a single sentence describing a possible improvement.

quests.title: Find one tiny friction — daily practice
quests.description: Good design starts with noticing. Turn an everyday frustration into a possibility. Try a fresh idea each day.
steps: Notice one thing on campus that could be easier.
Write down who it affects and why it matters.
Sketch one possible solution on paper. Keep it simple.

quests.title: Catch a tiny tool idea
quests.description: A two-minute step is enough. You can return to this practice every day.
steps: Think of one repetitive task you do.
Write one sentence about a tool that could help.

quests.title: Sketch your tiny tool — daily practice
quests.description: Before the first line of code, give your idea a little shape. Try a fresh idea each day.
steps: Choose a small problem you or a friend faces.
Write one sentence describing your tool.
Draw the main screen and label its three most useful features.

quests.title: Make one greener choice
quests.description: A two-minute step is enough. You can return to this practice every day.
steps: Pick one reusable item you can use today.
Use it instead of a disposable alternative.

quests.title: Spot a greener possibility — daily practice
quests.description: Small observations can grow into meaningful change. Try a fresh idea each day.
steps: Find one place on campus where resources are wasted.
Write down a practical improvement.
List one person or campus group who could help.

quests.title: Write a little kindness
quests.description: A two-minute step is enough. You can return to this practice every day.
steps: Think of someone who made your day better.
Write two sentences about that moment in your notes.

quests.title: Write a six-sentence story — daily practice
quests.description: You do not need a whole novel to make someone feel something. Try a fresh idea each day.
steps: Choose a fictional student doing something kind.
Write six sentences: a beginning, a challenge, and a hopeful ending.
Read it aloud and improve one sentence.

quests.title: One tiny step: class
quests.description: Two minutes is enough to start. Try a fresh idea every day.
steps: Write down one concept you want to learn.
Save your note somewhere you can return to it.

quests.title: Outline a lesson
quests.description: A little focused practice for your next chapter. Use a fresh idea each day.
steps: Choose a concept related to your goal.
Read your own class notes or a textbook page.
Explain it in your own words and create one example.

quests.title: One tiny step: club
quests.description: Two minutes is enough to start. Try a fresh idea every day.
steps: Write one question you would ask a club member.
Save your note somewhere you can return to it.

quests.title: Bring an idea to the table
quests.description: A little focused practice for your next chapter. Use a fresh idea each day.
steps: Choose a club theme you would enjoy.
Draft a short introduction and an idea for a club activity.
Write three ways you could contribute using your current skills.

quests.title: One tiny step: certification
quests.description: Two minutes is enough to start. Try a fresh idea every day.
steps: Write down one technical skill you want to practice.
Save your note somewhere you can return to it.

quests.title: Plan your first learning sprint
quests.description: A little focused practice for your next chapter. Use a fresh idea each day.
steps: Choose a skill you want to build.
List three topics and design a practice exercise for each.
Set a realistic schedule and try the first exercise.

quests.title: One tiny step: local event
quests.description: Two minutes is enough to start. Try a fresh idea every day.
steps: Write one question you would bring to a career event.
Save your note somewhere you can return to it.

quests.title: Build your event game plan
quests.description: A little focused practice for your next chapter. Use a fresh idea each day.
steps: Choose a career topic that interests you.
Draft three questions and a short self-introduction.
Write a follow-up note template and rehearse it aloud.

quests.title: One tiny step: networking
quests.description: Two minutes is enough to start. Try a fresh idea every day.
steps: Write one sentence introducing yourself and your interests.
Save your note somewhere you can return to it.

quests.title: Practice your introduction
quests.description: A little focused practice for your next chapter. Use a fresh idea each day.
steps: Imagine a professional you would like to learn from.
Draft a thoughtful introduction and two specific questions.
Read it aloud and revise for clarity. Keep it as a private practice draft.

quests.title: One tiny step: job simulation
quests.description: Two minutes is enough to start. Try a fresh idea every day.
steps: Name one user and a problem a product could solve.
Save your note somewhere you can return to it.

quests.title: Be the product lead
quests.description: A little focused practice for your next chapter. Use a fresh idea each day.
steps: Imagine students need a better way to find study groups.
Describe a user, three needs, and one feature you would prioritize.
Write your decision and one simple metric to evaluate it.

quests.title: One tiny step: internship
quests.description: Two minutes is enough to start. Try a fresh idea every day.
steps: Write one accomplishment you could include in an application.
Save your note somewhere you can return to it.

quests.title: Draft your application story
quests.description: A little focused practice for your next chapter. Use a fresh idea each day.
steps: Choose a fictional role you might enjoy.
Draft a short paragraph with one concrete accomplishment.
Identify one missing skill and create a practice plan to develop it.

quests.title: Find one tiny friction · hard
quests.description: Good design starts with noticing. Turn an everyday frustration into a possibility. Try a fresh idea each day.
steps: Notice one thing on campus that could be easier.
Write down who it affects and why it matters.
Sketch one possible solution on paper. Keep it simple.
Create a concrete first draft or prototype from your plan.
Review it and write down one improvement.
